headline: MLA Humayun Kabir announces retirement from politics over vote looting claims
summary: The Murshidabad MLA broke down in tears after being detained for 12 hours by police during a by-election in West Bengal.
details: Humayun Kabir, the MLA for Nauda in Murshidabad, indicated his retirement from politics following allegations of 'vote looting' during the by-election for the Rezinagar assembly seat.
caption:
A top leader of the Aam Aadmi Unnayan Party broke down in tears and announced his retirement from politics after alleging police-backed vote looting in West Bengal.

Humayun Kabir, the MLA for Nauda in Murshidabad, indicated his retirement from politics following allegations of 'vote looting' during the by-election for the Rezinagar assembly seat.

headline_marked: 3 [[fake CID officers jailed]] for demanding 10 lakh BDT extortion from jewelry shop
headline: 3 fake CID officers jailed for demanding 10 lakh BDT extortion from jewelry shop
summary: The suspects entered a jewelry store in Old Dhaka, posing as CID officers and threatening the owner's family over alleged hundi business.
details: A Dhaka court has sent three men to jail after they allegedly posed as Criminal Investigation Department (CID) officers to extort 10 lakh BDT from a gold shop in Tantibazar, Old Dhaka.
The suspects, identified as SM Mostaq Ahmed (65), Md. Hasan Sheikh (38), and Md. Abul Kalam Azad (52), entered the 'Ashirbad' jewelry store on Tuesday and threatened the owner's brother and son.
The imposters claimed the shop was involved in illegal hundi business and demanded 10 lakh BDT, threatening to arrest the family members if the money was not paid.

The shop owner, Liton Deb, immediately notified the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police. A DB team led by Additional Deputy Commissioner Md. Enayet Kabir Soeb caught the three men red-handed at the scene.
Police seized a grey CID jacket, a pair of handcuffs, and a sealed identification card from the suspects during the arrest.
The investigating officer, SI Md. Ejazul Huq of Kotwali Police Station, has requested a 10-day remand for the suspects to uncover the details of the ring and identify other accomplices.
While the suspects used CID and police identities, the investigating officer stated that their actual identities are still being verified as the investigation continues.
caption:
Posing as CID officers, three men tried to extort 10 lakh BDT from a jewelry shop owner in Old Dhaka.

A Dhaka court has sent three men to jail after they allegedly posed as Criminal Investigation Department (CID) officers to extort 10 lakh BDT from a gold shop in Tantibazar, Old Dhaka.

The suspects, identified as SM Mostaq Ahmed (65), Md. Hasan Sheikh (38), and Md. Abul Kalam Azad (52), entered the 'Ashirbad' jewelry store on Tuesday and threatened the owner's brother and son.

The imposters claimed the shop was involved in illegal hundi business and demanded 10 lakh BDT, threatening to arrest the family members if the money was not paid.

The shop owner, Liton Deb, immediately notified the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police. A DB team led by Additional Deputy Commissioner Md. Enayet Kabir Soeb caught the three men red-handed at the scene.

Police seized a grey CID jacket, a pair of handcuffs, and a sealed identification card from the suspects during the arrest.

The investigating officer, SI Md. Ejazul Huq of Kotwali Police Station, has requested a 10-day remand for the suspects to uncover the details of the ring and identify other accomplices.

While the suspects used CID and police identities, the investigating officer stated that their actual identities are still being verified as the investigation continues.
